headline: Two independent USD implementations agree on the graded scene (G2 pass) and the headless llvmpipe render puts every mesh exactly where the independent numpy pinhole oracle says (0.0654 of pixels drawn).

gates.name: G1
gates.measured: both readers see exactly 5 meshes, 1 camera, a lit light; no forbidden arc/schema/property
gates.threshold: exactly 5 meshes, exactly 1 camera, >= 1 light with inputs:intensity > 0, no forbidden arc

gates.name: G2
gates.measured: the two readers agree on the prim set, point counts, world transforms and world bboxes

gates.name: G4
gates.measured: every mesh lands where the independent numpy pinhole oracle says, painted its declared colour
gates.threshold: area >= 400 px^2, >= 90% on screen, overlap <= 10%, k in [0.06, 1.30], dev <= 0.35

numbers.label: mutants killed by a named judge gate
judge tree unchanged by the graded run

hero.caption: The graded render, the real llvmpipe orbit, and the judge verdict and mutant kill matrix.

gallery.caption: Graded render with the G4 oracle rectangles and the measured per-mesh illuminance k.
Grade verdict per iteration plus the self-test kill matrix.

launch.ask_agent:
Read `cookbook/nanousd-render/SPEC.md` and write `my_scene.usda` that passes
`bash cookbook/nanousd-render/judge/grade.sh my_scene.usda` with exit 0. First
run `bash cookbook/nanousd-render/judge/setup.sh` once to install the pinned
tools. Iterate: author or fix the scene yourself, grade it, read the JSON
verdict (it names the gate and the exact number that failed — a mesh out of
frame, a color too close to another, a camera the two readers disagree on),
and fix your scene until every gate passes. Do not edit anything under
`judge/` — the judge hashes its own tree and fails closed if it changed.
